subject: Hosted API token tiers — request for durable price protections
messages:
From: Tom Park <tom@edisonlabs.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Edison Labs Procurement <procurement@edisonlabs.io>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Initial usage/discount ask + price protection question

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile and the prefix caching looks like it would shave a lot off our per-call cost. Before we move deeper, Procurement asked for a couple of things we need clarified for our internal approval:

- A tiered per-token discount schedule for hosted API usage (we expect a 12-month ramp: 50M tokens month 1, 250M by month 6, 600M+ by month 12). Forecast attached (EDSL-MVP-usage-forecast.xlsx).
- Durable price protections: our finance team prefers a 12-month price lock on per-token rates after signing; alternatively, an annual CPI cap or an MFN clause if you introduce lower public pricing to comparable customers.

Could you share what Redwood typically offers for hosted, usage-based commitments at this scale and what level of price protection is on the table? Also copying our procurement alias.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
Edison Labs


From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Park <tom@edisonlabs.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial usage/discount ask + price protection question

Tom — really appreciate the clear forecast and the time yesterday. I reviewed the numbers with Aditya (sales lead) and Neha (revops). High-level thoughts:

- Commitment/discount construct we usually recommend: a stepped per-token price tied to committed monthly/quarterly volumes with a minimum committed ARR for promotional pricing.
- For 12-month ramp like yours, we can propose three commit tiers (base: 100M/mo, growth: 300M/mo, scale: 600M+/mo) with blended effective discounts that increase as you hit tiers.
- Regarding price protections: Redwood is willing to provide a 12-month price lock on the per-token rate for the committed tiers, subject to standard carve-outs (e.g., changes in public cloud pricing beyond X% or fiscal/regulatory passes). We can also discuss an annual CPI cap instead of an absolute lock if that helps internal finance.

I'll attach an initial sketch of a commercial term sheet and the forecast — Neha will model the blended effective rates. Can we get a sense of whether Edison needs MFN specifically or if a firm 12-month lock + CPI cap would be sufficient?

Next steps: Neha will push a spreadsheet back with modeled per-token rates and an alternate version that includes a limited MFN-style protection (customer must request MFN in the first 30 days post-signature).

Best,
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: EDSL-MVP-usage-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet; 47KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Park <tom@edisonlabs.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial usage/discount ask + price protection question

Tom — attached is the modeled pricing deck with two scenarios:

Scenario A — 12-month price lock on committed tiers (no MFN):
- Tier 1 (100–299M/mo): $0.00015 per token
- Tier 2 (300–599M/mo): $0.00012 per token
- Tier 3 (600M+/mo): $0.000095 per token
- Lock applies to per-token rates for 12 months post-signature.

Scenario B — 12-month lock + limited MFN window:
- Same base tiers; MFN triggers if Redwood publicly publishes a materially lower price for the same model + SLA within 180 days of signing AND the customer execution footprint meets a minimum commit. MFN would be limited to a single downward true-up and would not apply to promotional or one-off marketplace discounts.

CPI cap option: If Edison prefers, we can replace the absolute lock with a 12-month CPI cap (cap = CPI + 3%).

I also included an alternative where we provide a partial credit for retroactive lower prices (true-up credit applied to future invoices, limited to the committed term).

Attachment: commercial-term-sketch.pdf (PDF; 120KB)

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the scenarios.

-Neha
Senior Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Park <tom@edisonlabs.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Edison Labs Procurement <procurement@edisonlabs.io>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial usage/discount ask + price protection question

Thanks Neha — the scenarios look reasonable. A few clarifying points from our CFO and procurement: 

1) The CFO prefers a concrete 12-month price lock rather than CPI-linked adjustments; they want predictable unit costs for budgeting.
2) MFN is important to us because we run a public comparison model and need protection against tiered promotional pricing for similar enterprise accounts. However, procurement is open to a limited MFN window (180 days) and a single true-up if Redwood publishes a lower, materially equivalent price.
3) We need the carve-outs spelled out clearly: specifically, marketplace promotions (e.g., first-90-day AWS marketplace credits), small-volume pilot discounts, and special multi-year enterprise-only discounts should be excluded from MFN.

Can your legal team put together a short section we can add to our SOW/Contract that captures: 12-month price lock on per-token rates for the committed tiers; MFN window 180 days with single true-up credit; exclusions list as above; and a process for initiating a true-up (notice period, evidence required, credit application)?

If you can produce that language quickly we can move to internal sign-off and finalize the commercial annex.

Best,
Tom

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial usage/discount ask + price protection question

Tom — Markus from Redwood Legal here. Thanks for the clear direction. Below is a concise draft clause you can insert in the commercial annex / SOW. Happy to iterate.

DRAFT PRICE PROTECTION CLAUSE (for inclusion in Annex X — Pricing):
1. Price Lock: Redwood agrees that, for a period of twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, the per-token rates for services provided under this Agreement for the committed volume tiers referenced in Annex Y shall not increase above the rates set forth in Annex Y.
2. MFN True-up: For a period of one hundred eighty (180) days following the Effective Date, if Redwood publicly offers materially lower published per-token rates for substantially similar hosted API offerings and materially similar Service Levels to any third party, Customer may request a single retrospective true-up credit equal to the difference between the rates paid by Customer and the materially lower published rate, applied to future invoices. The MFN provision shall not apply to: (a) promotional marketplace credits or short-term marketplace promotions; (b) pilot or small-volume introductory discounts below the threshold of Annex Y; (c) custom multi-year enterprise agreements negotiated separately with distinct scope.
3. True-up Process: Customer shall provide written notice identifying the publicly offered lower rate and supporting evidence. Redwood shall have thirty (30) days to confirm and, if applicable, apply the true-up credit within the next two billing cycles.
4. Exclusions & Force Majeure: Standard carve-outs apply for changes to cloud provider fees, third-party licensing cost increases beyond Redwood's control, and applicable law/regulatory changes.

If that reads OK I can produce a tracked version suitable for insertion. Let me know and we'll also include the redlines around the retroactive credit calculation.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Edison_RFP_Security_Excerpt.pdf (PDF; 230KB)
